question.problem:
Find the smallest natural number solution to the system of linear congruences below.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x≡2 & (\text{mod}\,3) \\ x≡3 & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since $3$ and $5$ are coprime, then according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $3\cdot 5=15.$

From the first congruence, we get

$$
x≡2\,(\text{mod}\,3)\,⟹\,x=2+3t,\,t\in Z.
$$

Substituting this into the second congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5) \\ 2+3t & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5) \\ 3t & ≡1 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $5$ is a relatively small modulus, by trial and error, we have that $2\cdot 3≡1\,(\text{mod}\,5).$ So, we multiply both sides by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3t & ≡1 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5) \\ 2\cdot 3t & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5) \\ t & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $t=2+5s,$ where $s\in Z.$ Substituting this into the expression for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2+3t \\  & =2+3(2+5s) \\  & =8+15s.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x≡8\,(\text{mod}\,15)$ is the unique solution modulo $15,$ and $x=8$ is the smallest natural number solution to the system.
